items.followUp: Define a problem and name three details that should be identified before solving it.

rubric.why: A problem must be clearly stated, including what is to be achieved.
rubric.description: Explains what defining a problem means.
rubric.how: Award for stating that it clearly describes the problem or its goal.

rubric.why: Identifying inputs and expected outputs, or gathering relevant information, helps clarify the problem.
rubric.description: Gives a useful strategy for understanding the problem.
rubric.how: Award for identifying inputs and outputs or asking questions/gathering information.

rubric.why: Constraints and unknowns help establish the problem's limits and needs.
rubric.description: Identifies constraints, requirements, or unknowns.
rubric.how: Award for naming a relevant limit, requirement, or unknown.

rubric.why: Breaking the problem into smaller parts or separating knowns from unknowns makes it easier to solve.
rubric.description: Gives another strategy for defining or analysing the problem.
rubric.how: Award for a distinct strategy such as decomposition or identifying known and unknown information.

modelAnswer: Defining a problem means stating clearly what needs to be solved and what the desired result is.
Ask questions and gather information about the problem.
Identify the inputs, expected outputs, and requirements.
Identify constraints and unknowns, and break a complex problem into smaller parts.

items.followUp: Describe how data travels in a star topology and name one device at its centre.

rubric.why: A bus topology is organised around one shared main cable.
rubric.description: Defines the central cable arrangement.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the single main cable or backbone.

rubric.why: Each computer or device connects to the shared cable.
rubric.description: Explains how devices are connected.
rubric.how: Award for stating that devices/nodes attach to the main cable.

rubric.why: Data sent on the bus travels along the cable and is available to connected devices.
rubric.description: Explains how data is transmitted.
rubric.how: Award for describing data travelling along the bus or being broadcast to connected devices.

rubric.why: Terminators at the cable ends prevent signals from reflecting back along the bus.
rubric.description: Mentions the purpose of terminators.
rubric.how: Award for naming terminators and their role at the ends of the cable.

modelAnswer: In a bus topology, all computers and other devices are connected to one main cable called the bus or backbone.
When a device sends data, the signal travels along the shared cable and can be received by the connected devices.
The intended device accepts the data; the other devices ignore it.
Terminators at both ends of the cable absorb signals and prevent them from reflecting back.

items.followUp: Write a short note on privacy and responsible behaviour when using computer networks.

rubric.why: Protecting personal and confidential information is an important security responsibility.
rubric.description: Mentions privacy and protection of information.
rubric.how: Award for identifying privacy or safeguarding personal/confidential data.

rubric.why: Accessing systems or data without permission is unethical.
rubric.description: Identifies unauthorised access as an ethical issue.
rubric.how: Award for mentioning hacking, unauthorised access, or the need for permission.

rubric.why: Data theft, misuse, or improper sharing violates the rights of its owner.
rubric.description: Mentions responsible handling and ownership of data.
rubric.how: Award for identifying data theft, misuse, or sharing without permission.

rubric.why: Users should avoid harmful actions and help protect systems from security threats.
rubric.description: Gives another ethical security responsibility.
rubric.how: Award for a valid point such as not spreading malware or reporting security threats.

modelAnswer: Ethical issues related to security concern the responsible protection and use of computer systems and information.
Users should respect privacy and keep personal or confidential information safe.
Accessing, copying, changing, or sharing another person's data without permission is unethical.
Users should not create or spread malware and should report security threats responsibly.

items.followUp: Name the two main resources used to assess an algorithm's efficiency.

rubric.why: The time an algorithm takes to run is one measure of efficiency.
rubric.description: Names time or execution-time efficiency.
rubric.how: Award for identifying running/execution time.

rubric.why: The memory an algorithm uses is another measure of efficiency.
rubric.description: Names memory or space efficiency.
rubric.how: Award for identifying memory/space usage.

modelAnswer: The efficiency of an algorithm is measured by the time it takes to execute and the memory (space) it uses.

items.followUp: What is one example of an input and an expected output for a well-defined problem?

rubric.why: A well-defined problem has a clear and precise goal.
rubric.description: States that the problem is clearly described.
rubric.how: Award for describing its goal or requirements as clear and precise.

rubric.why: The information provided and the expected result should be identifiable.
rubric.description: Mentions identifiable inputs and outputs or expected results.
rubric.how: Award for stating that inputs and outputs/results are known or specified.

modelAnswer: A well-defined problem is one that is stated clearly and precisely, with its goal, requirements, inputs, and expected output identifiable.

items.followUp: Name two data types used to store whole numbers and characters.

rubric.why: Float is a real-number data type.
rubric.description: Names the float real data type.
rubric.how: Award for writing float.

rubric.why: Double is another real-number data type, typically allowing greater precision.
rubric.description: Names the double real data type.
rubric.how: Award for writing double.

modelAnswer: Two real data types are float and double.

items.followUp: Explain how acting out a problem can help you find its solution.

rubric.why: The strategy involves physically demonstrating or role-playing the situation.
rubric.description: Explains what the act-it-out strategy involves.
rubric.how: Award for describing a physical demonstration, simulation, or role-play.

rubric.why: Acting out makes events or steps easier to understand and can reveal a solution.
rubric.description: Explains how the strategy helps solve the problem.
rubric.how: Award for linking the demonstration to understanding the steps, events, or solution.

modelAnswer: In the “Act it Out” strategy, a person physically demonstrates or role-plays the situation in the problem.
This makes the events and their order easier to understand and can help reveal a solution.

items.followUp: What is the purpose of the href attribute in an HTML anchor tag?

rubric.why: Attributes provide extra information or set properties for an HTML element.
rubric.description: Defines the purpose of attributes in HTML tags.
rubric.how: Award for stating that attributes give additional information or specify an element's properties.

rubric.why: Attributes are written in the opening tag as name-value pairs, such as href in an anchor tag.
rubric.description: Gives the position or a valid example of an attribute.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the name=value form or giving a correct HTML attribute example.

modelAnswer: Attributes provide additional information about an HTML element or set its properties.
They are written in the opening tag as name-value pairs, for example, <a href="page.html">.
